functional.description: Show a local panel catalog of every implemented chat command with syntax, purpose, supported roles, and whether access can be changed.
functional.rationale: The streamer needs one complete reference and control surface.

functional.description: Allow the streamer to configure an explicit allowlist of roles for each mutable command and persist the same policy used by panel help and chat authorization.
functional.rationale: One source of truth avoids the catalog promising access that execution denies.

functional.description: Keep the initial policy consistent with existing access: self-service commands and read-only global commands stay available to everyone; existing management access stays with streamer and moderator, with VIP access gated by the existing toggle.
functional.rationale: Configurable policy must not silently change current channel behavior.

functional.description: Keep !conta <nome> and !conta reset immutable and streamer-only in chat, panel metadata, and API validation.
functional.rationale: These account-label controls are explicitly reserved for the streamer.

functional.description: Support global command discovery through !queue comandos, returning all commands available across the product using the same persisted policy; direct the streamer to the panel. Keep !<fila> comandos for queue-specific help.
functional.rationale: Viewers and moderators need role-specific help without exposing unavailable controls.

functional.description: Recognize streamer identity, current-message moderator/VIP/subscriber badges, and the everyone role; VIP grants remain disabled unless the existing VIP-management toggle is enabled.
functional.rationale: Authorization must use trustworthy Twitch event data and preserve the existing VIP safety switch.

functional.description: Ensure denied commands and hidden command discovery produce no queue lookup, mutation, account lookup, or external API call beyond the minimal work required to identify the queue help response.
functional.rationale: Authorization denials must not trigger side effects or reveal protected operations.

functional.description: Keep help responses within existing chat cooldown and 500-character limits and provide a concise Portuguese empty/denied response appropriate to the sender role.
functional.rationale: Chat help must be usable without flooding or disclosing hidden commands.

functional.description: Provide global !queue ping restricted immutably to streamer and moderators; reply with Pong, a ping-pong emoji, running version and latest cached Twitch API latency.
functional.rationale: Operator can verify chat response and recent Twitch connectivity from chat.

functional.description: Reserve queue as a global command namespace so no queue slug or alias can shadow !queue comandos or !queue ping.
functional.rationale: Global commands need unambiguous parsing and authorization.

nonFunctional.description: Only the authenticated local panel can read or change the command catalog policy; all mutations continue through session, CSRF, operation-idempotency, and schema checks.
nonFunctional.metric: Unauthenticated/cross-site mutations rejected; streamer-only roles cannot be relaxed by any request.

nonFunctional.description: Persist policy across bot restarts and use a single source of truth for rendering help and authorizing commands.
nonFunctional.metric: Real PostgreSQL migration-backed integration tests pass across repository reconstruction.

nonFunctional.description: Panel and chat copy remain pt-BR and distinguish configurable from immutable command access.
nonFunctional.metric: All user-visible catalog and help labels are Portuguese and fit the existing 500-character chat limit.

constraints.description: Application remains JavaScript ESM, Fastify, vanilla frontend, PostgreSQL and Prisma; no additional runtime service or dependency is introduced.
constraints.impact: Use existing modules, setting persistence and panel navigation patterns.

constraints.description: Configurable role set is streamer, moderator, VIP, subscriber, and everyone, with VIP controlled by the existing global toggle; follower is excluded from v1.
constraints.impact: Do not add the Twitch followers scope or infer follower status.

constraints.description: Multiple allowed roles use explicit OR semantics without hierarchy inheritance; the streamer retains access except for no command, while streamer-only commands remain locked to streamer.
constraints.impact: A user may match multiple current-event badges; matching any configured eligible role allows the command.

constraints.description: The initial policy preserves current access, except !conta <nome> and !conta reset become streamer-only; !queue ping is fixed to streamer and moderator.
constraints.impact: Seed default behavior and fixed audiences.

constraints.description: !queue ping reads only the latest in-process health probe cache and does not perform a Twitch API request for each command.
constraints.impact: Share safe health snapshot with chat handler and show unavailable when no probe exists.

assumptions.description: The existing local-panel session represents the streamer/operator; the command policy UI is not a public control surface.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: An additional operator role/access-control model would be required.

assumptions.description: Twitch chat events expose current moderator, VIP, and subscriber badges and the current broadcaster identity.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Some configurable roles would need a different data source and explicit scope review.

interactions.trigger: Streamer opens the Comandos panel page
flow: Fetch the command catalog and effective persisted policy
Render descriptions, syntax, allowed roles, and locked streamer-only commands
Refresh the same effective policy used by the chat handler

states.error: Show a safe Portuguese error and preserve current selections
states.empty: Show an explicit no-commands state only if the catalog is empty

interactions.trigger: Viewer, subscriber, VIP, moderator, or streamer sends !queue comandos
flow: Return all permitted command syntax or direct streamer to panel
Apply viewer cooldown and message limit

states.empty: Explain that no commands are available to this role

interactions.trigger: Streamer or target-channel moderator sends !queue ping
flow: Read cached Twitch API latency and running product version
Reply Pong 🏓 with version and latency without calling Helix

states.error: Show latency unavailable if no probe is cached

edgeCases.scenario: An API request attempts to add a non-streamer role to an immutable command
edgeCases.handling: Reject before persistence and return a safe validation error; preserve current policy.

edgeCases.scenario: A user has multiple trusted badges, such as moderator and subscriber
edgeCases.handling: Authorize when any eligible role in the explicit allowlist matches; VIP still requires the existing toggle.

edgeCases.scenario: Subscriber badge is absent, stale, or supplied only by another broadcaster in Shared Chat
edgeCases.handling: Use only badges and identity from the current target-channel event; never persist/reuse badge state and reject wrong-channel events.

edgeCases.scenario: Persisted policy is missing, malformed, or has a newer version than submitted
edgeCases.handling: Use a safe built-in default only when no record exists; reject malformed/conflicting writes and do not open permissions implicitly.

edgeCases.scenario: A role has no eligible commands or the help response would exceed 500 characters
edgeCases.handling: Return concise Portuguese no-access or a bounded syntax list with a panel hint.

edgeCases.scenario: Ping arrives before a health probe has produced Twitch latency
edgeCases.handling: Still reply Pong and version, label latency unavailable, and do not initiate a network request.

terminology.definition: Allowlist role that permits the command to any sender, including users with other badges.
avoid: viewer role implying every command is safe

terminology.definition: Role badge included in the Twitch EventSub chat message currently being authorized.
Command that only the broadcaster identity may execute and that the panel/API cannot broaden.
